mentalMap.label: Two families
mentalMap.sub: symmetric = one shared secret, fast, key-distribution problem · asymmetric = key pair, public half free, slow

mentalMap.label: Cipher vs key
mentalMap.sub: cipher is the published algorithm, key is the secret — real systems are hybrid

mentalMap.label: Block vs stream
mentalMap.sub: AES 128-bit block, 10/12/14 rounds (bulk) · ChaCha20 keystream (streaming, no AES hardware)

mentalMap.label: Mode + padding
mentalMap.sub: GCM/CTR/CBC stop identical blocks matching; PKCS#7 pads to a whole block

mentalMap.label: Modular arithmetic
mentalMap.sub: Z_p · FLT a^(p-1)≡1 (mod p) · group order p-1 · generator g

mentalMap.label: Diffie-Hellman
mentalMap.sub: publish A=g^a, B=g^b → secret B^a = A^b = g^(ab) mod p — computed, never sent

mentalMap.label: Hash properties
mentalMap.sub: deterministic · fixed length · one-way · avalanche · collision-resistant

mentalMap.label: SHA-256 pipeline
mentalMap.sub: pad (1 bit + zeros + 64-bit length) → n = ceil((L+9)/64) blocks → 64-word schedule → 64 rounds → 256-bit digest

mentalMap.label: Where SHA sits
mentalMap.sub: txn hash → Merkle root → header hash → next header's link — tampering breaks every later hash

drill: Name the four objectives of cryptography.
Confidentiality, integrity, authentication, non-repudiation
Which mechanism alone gives non-repudiation?
Digital signature — a shared symmetric key lets either party forge
What is the key-distribution problem?
Getting a shared secret to a second party over an untrusted channel
Why do real systems use a hybrid?
Asymmetric wraps a random symmetric session key; asymmetric alone is too slow
What block size does AES use, and how many rounds per key size?
128-bit block; 10 rounds AES-128, 12 AES-192, 14 AES-256
Why does AES run inside a mode?
The mode stops identical plaintext blocks producing identical ciphertext blocks; GCM adds an auth tag
State Fermat's little theorem.
For prime p and a not divisible by p: a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p)
Diffie-Hellman with p=23, g=5, a=6, b=15 — what are A, B and the secret?
A = 8, B = 19, shared secret = 2
Why is the secret not A × B mod p?
Exponents combine multiplicatively: the secret is g^(ab) mod p
What problem is Diffie-Hellman security based on?
The discrete logarithm problem — recovering x from g^x mod p
Name the five cryptographic hash properties.
Deterministic, fixed length, one-way, avalanche, collision-resistant
How long is a SHA-256 digest?
256 bits = 32 bytes = 64 hex characters
How many blocks for a 100-byte message?
How many blocks for a 55-byte message, and why?
1 block — 55 + 1 + 8 = 64 bytes exactly fills it
State the SHA-256 padding rule.
1 bit, then zeros to 448 mod 512, then the 64-bit original length
What is SHA-256('abc')?
What is hashed to make a block hash?
The block header — transactions enter only through the Merkle root
What does the Merkle root commit to?
All transactions in the block, via their hashes
What happens if one transaction is altered?
Root changes → header hash changes → every later link fails verification
Why hash blocks rather than sign them?
Hashing is free for anyone to verify and needs no key; signing proves authorship, not integrity
Why is a checksum unsafe as a block identifier?
CRC-style checksums detect accidental corruption only; collisions are trivially crafted
